subject: Production surge: reserved capacity request and allocation plan
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@orionai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Production surge + reserved capacity request

Hi Jordan,

Quick heads up — we have a major user acquisition campaign that lands the week of April 15 and our traffic forecasts show a ~6x spike in inference QPS for roughly 10 days (attached). We are currently on your shared hosted tier but the risk of preemption during the window is a blocker for the campaign.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood reserve dedicated capacity (A100-equivalent) to guarantee throughput for the campaign window?
- If reservation isn’t possible, what is the fastest path to ensure we won’t be preempted (burst, higher priority lane, or canary routing)?

We’re ready to sign a short-term commitment if that helps lock capacity. We need an answer this week to finalize our marketing plan.

Attached: orion_surge_forecast_q2.csv (traffic forecast).

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of Platform
OrionAI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production surge + reserved capacity request

Forwarding Sarah's note — asks for guaranteed throughput during a targeted 10-day campaign window (wk of Apr 15). Need quick triage and decision. High level options below; please weigh constraints and confirm by EOD so I can get back to them.

Options (initial):
1) Short-term Dedicated reservation: carve 2 x A100-equivalent slots in Aurora pool, reserved Apr 14–25.
   - Pros: deterministic latency, avoids preemption.
   - Cons: consumes scarce pool capacity; potential pushback from other committed deals.
2) Burst lane + priority routing: keep in shared pool but set priority weight and 15–25% burst allocation for the window.
   - Pros: lower upfront cost, flexible.
   - Cons: not fully guaranteed under extreme contention.
3) Model/quantization mitigation: run quantized variant on lower-memory nodes; coupled with prefix caching to reduce QPS.
   - Pros: less capacity hit overall.
   - Cons: requires validating quality/regression risk.

Questions:
- Marissa: what does the April calendar look like in Aurora? any existing reserves that conflict?
- Vivek: is leadership comfortable approving a short reserve for a new mid-tier Strategic (likely to expand) account?
- Ben: commercial — are they willing to convert to a short-term commit? any deal momentum?

I’ll assemble numbers once you give pros/cons. If we take option 1 we should also attach a temporary canary (ramp) and an SLA credit if preempted during the window.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production surge + reserved capacity request

Jordan — thanks for the ping. Quick sales perspective:
- Orion is a mid/upper-mid account with clear expansion potential; converting this campaign to a short-term dedicated commitment is an upsell opportunity (deal id ORN-4721).
- I’ll push a short-term quote for 2 reserved slots for the Apr 14–25 window with a 20% burst buffer. See attached draft quote (ORN-4721-dedicated-quote.pdf).
- We should offer a reduced-term monthly commit and a slightly higher burst to keep them comfortable.

One thing to flag: LumenTech has a campaign that overlaps Apr 12–18 and they currently have a partial reserve in Aurora. We need the capacity calendar check before we commit anything. If Aurora is tight, offer Orion a dedicated tranche in the east pool we were planning to bring online for Q2.

I’ll start commercial terms and pull legal for a short amendment.

—Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production surge + reserved capacity request — infra assessment

Quick infra readout after checking Aurora pool and Q2 calendar:
- Aurora pool has nominal headroom but Apr 12–18 is constrained: we have a partial reserve for LumenTech and a planned internal scale test on Apr 16. If we carve 2 full A100 slots for Orion in Aurora, we will push one of the smaller reserves (internal test) to the east pool. This is feasible but not without coordination.

Recommendation: two-phase approach
1) Reserve 1 dedicated slot in Aurora and 1 in East-tranche (hot-standby) for Apr 14–25. This reduces immediate contention and minimizes churn.
2) For traffic spikes, automatically route Orion traffic to a quantized variant (v1q) on lower-memory nodes — we should validate quality but latency will be within SLO for most queries.

Operational notes:
- We can program routing policy: priority weight = 0.9 for Orion on the designated reserved pool, with 15% burst cap.
- Canary plan: ramp 10% traffic for first 12 hours, full switch by hour 36 if stable.

Attachments: q2-capacity-heatmap.png, node-list-aurora-pool.txt

Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@orionai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production surge + reserved capacity request — decision and next steps

Sarah — thanks for the details and the forecast. Internal summary and decision below.

What we will do for the Apr 14–25 campaign window:
- Reserve two A100-equivalent slots for Orion (one in Aurora, one in East-tranche hot-standby) for Apr 14–25.
- Configure priority routing with weight 0.9 and a 15% burst allowance.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic for first 12 hours, ramp to full traffic by hour 36 if metrics look good.
- Quantized fallback (v1q) enabled for non-critical queries to reduce load; we will run a quick quality check before the run.
- Commercial: short-term commit (ORN-4721) with a documented one-time reserve fee; Ben will send the DocuSign and quote.
- SLA: we will include a one-off SLA credit in the event of preemption during Apr 14–25.

Next actions:
- Ben: send the amended quote + DocuSign link (today).
- Marissa: finalize routing policy and node assignment; run the quantized regression check with Orion staging by Mar 6.
- Laura/Vivek: approve temporary reserve (I recommend yes; we’re on a reasonable upsell path).

Proposed kickoff call: Mar 3, 10:00 PT — Ben will join with CS and Infra.

Links: DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/ORN-4721-quote), shared kickoff folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-orion-kickoff)

Attachments: commit-sla-summary.pdf

Sarah — can you confirm the Apr 14–25 window and that the staging team can do the regression test by Mar 6? Once you confirm, Ben will send DocuSign and we’ll lock the reservation.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Account Expansion
Redwood Inference
